milestones.title: M0 Stabilize
milestones.goal: Make the live app safe and dependable before we add more. Background jobs run on a schedule (a Vercel cron calls /api/internal/jobs with CRON_SECRET), so brand owners no longer need developer test buttons; those buttons are then hidden. Owners pick dates and times with normal pickers in their own timezone instead of typing ISO strings. CI checks every pull request again, and the seed test accounts are removed from production.
milestones.doneWhen: A queued job on the live app finishes without anyone pressing a button, no owner screen shows a test button or an ISO time field, every PR shows a green CI check, and production has no @grey-retention.test accounts.

milestones.title: M1 Design system
milestones.goal: Give Grey Retention its own calm, editorial, research-grade look (docs/DESIGN.md): warm off-white canvas, near-black ink, one electric-blue accent, an editorial serif for titles, Geist for UI and Geist Mono for labels and numbers, 4px corners and hairline borders. Apply it to the shell, navigation, buttons, forms, cards, tables and empty/loading/error states, and build the signature composer box.
milestones.doneWhen: Every owner, admin and designer screen uses the shared tokens and components, there are no leftover old colours or pill buttons, the composer component exists, and screens pass WCAG AA contrast, keyboard and 375px checks.

milestones.title: M1.5 Old-app UI rebuild
milestones.goal: Rebuild every screen of the old app 1:1 in structure and behaviour from docs/UI_REBUILD_SPEC.md (layout) and docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md (behaviour, wording, edge cases; its §18 simplification decisions win): the shell and shared components, dashboard, Klaviyo detail pages, brand and store, campaign planner and modals, campaign drafts and editor, Ask GROS, competitor agent, support, settings, holidays, connections and profile. Colours, fonts and icons come from the new design tokens; the §0 layout facts (20px cards, 12px controls, 255px/56px sidebar, outlined icons) win where they differ. The §15 old-app bugs are fixed, not copied. Data comes from the fake providers with honest labels; nothing live is switched on. New from the owner walk-through: one campaign status system, a real owner Approve step, drafts merged into Campaigns, one "+ New" menu, Team, Request a Feature and a brand-mismatch guard.
milestones.doneWhen: Every checkbox in docs/UI_REBUILD_SPEC.md §2–§14 is ticked; each screen works at desktop and 375px with keyboard access; every §15 bug and every (fix) in docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md is built corrected; and the five owner jobs in its §1 pass as Playwright journeys.

milestones.title: M2 Onboarding
milestones.goal: A new brand owner goes from store URL to brand preview to one competitor to a first useful draft without help (ONB-001 to ONB-035). Every step is honest about what is real, can be skipped or resumed, and never creates duplicates.
milestones.doneWhen: All ONB P0 items are verified with tests, and a first-time owner can enter a store URL, confirm the brand, add one competitor and open a useful draft in one sitting.

milestones.title: M3 Competitor watch
milestones.goal: Owners add and watch 5 to 10 competitor brands. Grey Retention collects their real emails into a searchable library, shows honest collection states (Not subscribed, Awaiting confirmation, Collecting, No messages yet, Needs attention) and keeps every original email unchanged.
milestones.doneWhen: An owner can add a competitor, see its true collection state, and browse, filter and search its captured emails with correct dates and sources.

milestones.title: M4 Replication engine
milestones.goal: Turn any competitor email or sequence into the owner's own version with three named modes (Exact, Rebrand, Adapt), a side-by-side comparison with the original, product mapping, locks and an honest list of differences.
milestones.doneWhen: An owner can pick a captured email or sequence, choose Exact, Rebrand or Adapt, map products, compare original and result side by side and get an editable email that keeps its source lineage.

milestones.title: M5 Store + delivery
milestones.goal: Bring in the owner's real store data (Shopify products, offers and ads) and deliver finished emails to Klaviyo: live connect, one fixed footer and stable segment names per store, safe export and scheduling, and send-state reconciliation that never sends twice.
milestones.doneWhen: With the owner's OK, a draft uses real store products and offers, is exported or scheduled in Klaviyo with the store's canonical footer and audiences, and its sent state matches Klaviyo.

milestones.title: M6 Intelligence
milestones.goal: Help owners understand and outsmart competitors: observed sequences and playbooks, an MCP server so other AI agents can use Grey Retention, a learning loop that improves drafts from feedback, and the remaining admin console pages (Clients, Prompt engine, Templates).
milestones.doneWhen: Owners can see a competitor's observed sequences and playbook with evidence, an external agent can work through the MCP server with the same permissions, feedback measurably changes later drafts, and admins have working Clients, Prompt engine and Templates pages.

milestones.title: V2 S1 Block library
milestones.goal: VISION.md Step 1. Twenty coded email block types (no countdown) that pull the logo, colours and font from the brand kit, render as email-safe HTML at 600px with a web-safe font stack, work at 375px, and end in a footer with Klaviyo's required tags. A model's only job is to pick which of the 20 types a competitor section is. The designer workflow is retired (decision D3).
milestones.doneWhen: Gate: on 50 hand-labelled competitor sections the model picks the same block type at least 85% of the time, and the owner approves the list of 20 types.

milestones.title: V2 S2 Inspiration inbox
milestones.goal: VISION.md Step 2 with decision D4. Competitor emails arrive at a Gmail +alias per brand, are stored once with every image downloaded and a 600px screenshot, cut into sections from the HTML structure, labelled, and summarised per email (micro) and per brand (macro).
milestones.doneWhen: Gate: 200 emails ingested, auto-assigned to the right brand, sectioned and labelled, with a per-brand summary the owner reads and agrees with.

milestones.title: V2 S3 Brand kit + assembly
milestones.goal: VISION.md Step 3. The onboarding wizard (S3a) and email assembly (S3b): from a hand-written brief the AI picks a block sequence, fills product blocks from featurable products, writes copy and renders HTML; copy QA checks the facts sheet, banned words, the discount regex and the code list. Exact, Rebrand and Adapt modes follow decision D1.
milestones.doneWhen: Gate: 10 emails for the test brand; the owner scores at least 7 of 10 as 'would send as-is'.

milestones.title: V2 S4 Klaviyo push + QA
milestones.goal: VISION.md Step 4. Full QA as a hard block (links, codes, dates, products, size, 375px screenshot, copy, audience, timezone), then images, template and campaign pushed to Klaviyo as a draft; the ops dashboard.
milestones.doneWhen: Gate: 10 of 10 drafts land in Klaviyo with zero manual fixes.

milestones.title: V2 S5 Weekly approval
milestones.goal: VISION.md Step 5. One weekly approval per client: the week's campaigns with a mobile screenshot, date, offer and segment, Approve all or Change (two AI rounds, then a person), in the app and by email with signed single-use links; approved campaigns are scheduled; '% approved without edits' is tracked.
milestones.doneWhen: Gate: a real client (not the test brand) approves 3 weeks through it without messaging us.

milestones.title: V2 S6 Brief + calendar
milestones.goal: VISION.md Step 6. An evidence-cited brief and a calendar built from competitor data, the client's own Klaviyo results and founder inputs, inside every guardrail.
milestones.doneWhen: Gate: the AI brief for the test brand, read next to the Step 0 manual brief, is at least as useful.

milestones.title: V2 S7 Three real clients
milestones.goal: VISION.md Step 7. Three real clients for one month; track one number, the share of emails approved without edits.
milestones.doneWhen: Gate: at least 70% of emails approved without edits.

workItems.title: Scheduled job worker
workItems.problem: Queued jobs (rewrites, imports, reports, planning) only run when someone presses a developer button or keeps a page open. `app/api/internal/jobs/route.ts` accepts only loopback fixture dispatch, so nothing runs on its own in production.
scope: Add a Vercel cron in `vercel.json` that calls `/api/internal/jobs` on a schedule with `Authorization: Bearer CRON_SECRET`.
Let the route run real queued jobs across workspaces in bounded batches (leases, retries and idempotency stay as they are); keep fixture-only dispatch for local fake mode.
Reject missing or wrong secrets; never expose the secret to the browser.
Tests: authorized run, unauthorized request, empty queue, failed job retried, lease not taken twice.
workItems.doneWhen: On the live app a queued job finishes within one cron interval without anyone pressing a button, and a request without the secret gets 401.

workItems.title: Hide developer test buttons from brand owners
workItems.problem: Owner screens show buttons such as "Run planning fixture jobs", "Run reference fixture jobs", "Run reporting fixture jobs" and "Run optimizer fixture jobs" (features/planning, references, reporting, optimizer, onboarding panels). They only exist because no worker runs jobs.
scope: Only after STAB-001 is live: remove these buttons from owner and staff screens, or show them only in local fake mode to platform admins.
Replace them with honest status text (Queued, Working, Done, Failed with retry).
Tests: owners never see the buttons in production mode; jobs still complete through the worker.
workItems.doneWhen: No owner or staff screen on the live app shows a "Run … jobs" button, and the work those buttons did still happens automatically.

workItems.title: Date and time pickers instead of typed ISO times
workItems.problem: Some forms ask owners to type values like `2026-11-01T10:00:00Z` (for example "Send time (ISO UTC …)" in `features/campaigns/editor.tsx` and "Rolling start (ISO timestamp with timezone)" in `features/planning/panels.tsx`).
scope: Replace every typed ISO field with date and time pickers in the workspace timezone, reusing the tested `lib/local-time.ts` conversion (skipped and repeated DST times).
Show times to owners as readable local text, never as ISO strings.
Tests: conversion across DST, invalid input, server-side validation, keyboard use and 375px layout.
workItems.doneWhen: No owner-facing form asks for an ISO time, and a time picked in the workspace timezone is saved and shown back as the same local time.

workItems.title: Re-enable CI on pull requests
workItems.problem: GitHub Actions is turned off for this repository, so `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (verify, database and browser jobs) has not run since October 28. Pull requests merge without an automatic check.
scope: Owner turns Actions back on (Settings → Actions → General → Allow all actions).
Confirm the verify, database and browser jobs pass on a pull request; fix or time-box the slow browser job so private-repo minutes stay affordable.
Make `verify` a required check on `main` (branch protection).
workItems.doneWhen: Every new pull request shows green verify, database and browser checks, and `main` cannot merge a red pull request.

workItems.title: Remove seed test accounts from production
workItems.problem: Synthetic seed users (`*@grey-retention.test`, for example owner, admin, designer, staff and other-owner) and their demo workspaces may exist in the live Supabase project.
scope: Read-only check of the live project first and a written list for Raman: which test accounts and workspaces exist and what they own.
With Raman's explicit OK, remove them with a reviewed, reversible script (backup first), keeping real accounts untouched.
Make sure seeds only run locally, never against production.
workItems.doneWhen: The live project has no `@grey-retention.test` users or their demo workspaces, real accounts are unchanged, and seeds cannot reach production.

workItems.title: One campaign status system
workItems.problem: Lane: **browser**. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §0.3 and §18.3: one draft showed up to five overlapping status vocabularies (WRITING / DRAFT pills, a Draft/Ready select, a WORKFLOW select, DRAFTS/READY/PUSHED filters, the calendar legend). Replace them with one system-driven status: Draft → With designer → Needs your approval → Scheduled → Sent (+ Cancelled, Missed). The same words appear on the calendar, the list view, the editor, the dashboard and filters.
scope: One status vocabulary in code, used by every screen; no manual status selects.
Status moves only through real events (assign, design delivered, owner approval, schedule, Klaviyo confirms the send).
Calendar legend, list filters and pills use the same words and colour roles (§0 of the spec).
Tests for every allowed transition and for refused ones (PT409 for business conflicts).
workItems.doneWhen: Every campaign shows exactly one status from the new set on every screen, statuses change only through real events, and tests cover each transition and each refused jump.

workItems.title: Owner Approve step before Schedule
workItems.problem: Lane: **browser**. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §0.2, Job 3, Job 4 and §18.4: the old app had no real owner approval. "Pending approval" was a dropdown value anyone could pick, and Schedule was a bare submit. Add an explicit owner Approve step (copy, then design) before Schedule, with a summary confirm: subject, from name, audience counts, and date and time with the brand timezone.
scope: Approve copy and Approve design actions for the brand owner only; staff and admins can't approve or skip the step.
Schedule stays blocked until both approvals, a future date and time, and a non-empty Send to.
Schedule opens a summary confirm; the time is shown with the one brand timezone.
Changing copy or design after approval asks again (the version is tied to the approval).
workItems.doneWhen: Only the owner can approve, Schedule is impossible without approval or with a past time or empty audience, and tests cover the owner, staff and admin paths.

workItems.title: Campaign drafts merged into Campaigns as its list view
workItems.problem: Lane: **browser**. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §0.5, §0.6 and §18.1: the drafts list had no sidebar entry and shared its title with the planner, and the planner's table view showed only half the campaigns. Merge the drafts list into Campaigns as its list view (calendar | list): one place for every campaign, local or Klaviyo, with one set of status filters.
scope: `/campaign-drafts` opens the Campaigns list view (redirect), keeping its status filter.
The list shows local drafts and synced Klaviyo campaigns, including Klaviyo drafts without a send time.
Filters use the UIR-015 status words; the calendar and the list always agree.
The sidebar highlights Campaigns on every campaign page.
workItems.doneWhen: Every campaign the calendar shows also appears in the list view, the old drafts URL lands there, and tests cover the merge, the filters and the empty state.

workItems.title: One "+ New" campaign menu
workItems.problem: Lane: **browser**. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §18.10: four similar toolbar buttons led to campaigns. Replace them with one "+ New" menu (Single send / Multi-day event / Fill the month with AI), and keep "+ plan send" on calendar cells as a shortcut.
scope: One keyboard-accessible "+ New" menu in the Campaigns toolbar, also on the dashboard and list view.
Each item opens the existing flow (New draft, multi-day wizard, calendar brief).
"+ plan send" opens the right date and never offers past days without a warning.
Rename the dashboard's "Schedule a campaign" link to "Create a campaign".
workItems.doneWhen: There is one "+ New" menu with three choices that reach the right flows, and tests cover keyboard use and each choice.

workItems.title: Team page
workItems.problem: Lane: **cloud**. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §14 (not in the UI spec): the Workspace group has a Team page at `/team` for members, invites and roles. Rename the Team role "Admin" to "Manager" (§18.17) so it no longer clashes with the platform admins who review designs.
scope: Follow every check in §14 of `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md`.
Invites and role changes go through server-authorized commands; no email is sent while providers are fake.
Owner-only actions are refused for other roles.
workItems.doneWhen: Every check in OWNER_JOURNEYS.md §14 passes, the role is called Manager, and tests cover invites, role changes, deactivation and refusals.

workItems.title: Request a Feature page
workItems.problem: Lane: **cloud**. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §15 (not in the UI spec): the Workspace group has Request a Feature at `/feedback`, where owners submit ideas and see what they asked for. The sidebar shows it as SOON until this page exists.
scope: Follow every check in §15 of `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md`.
Switch the sidebar item in `components/shell/nav-data.ts` from SOON to a link to `/feedback`.
Use "New request / Send" wording (§18.16).
workItems.doneWhen: Every check in OWNER_JOURNEYS.md §15 passes, the sidebar links to the page, and tests cover submit, validation and the empty state.

workItems.title: Brand-mismatch guard
workItems.problem: Lane: **cloud**. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §0.1 and §18.6: the old workspace ran for months on another brand's profile, site URL and product catalogue, so every AI feature was fed the wrong brand. Warn the owner when the brand profile, site URL or catalogue doesn't match the connected Klaviyo organisation, and point to the editable Brand profile to fix it.
scope: Compare brand profile, site URL and catalogue with the connected Klaviyo organisation (name, domain, currency, country) through the typed adapters.
Show a clear warning on Brand & Store and before AI generation; never block silently.
Fake-provider fixtures include a matching and a mismatching brand.
workItems.doneWhen: A mismatching workspace shows the warning before any AI step, a matching one doesn't, and tests cover both plus a missing connection.

workItems.title: Shared reference library component
workItems.problem: Lane: **cloud** builds it in UIR-009; the **browser** lane uses it in UIR-007. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §18 decision 12 and §7.2: the old app had three different reference pickers (New draft, the editor's design picker, the Inspiration page) with different tabs and counts ("Your Templates 0" in one place, uploads in another). Build one reference library component and use it everywhere.
scope: One component with the same tabs (yours, competitors, best picks) and the same counts wherever it appears.
Used by the New draft reference step, the editor's design picker and the Inspiration page.
Search and real thumbnails (sandboxed previews, links off); an empty tab says so plainly.
Cloud lane builds it inside UIR-009; the browser lane wires it into UIR-007.
workItems.doneWhen: New draft, the editor and Inspiration show the same library with the same tabs and counts, and tests cover search, empty tabs and picking a reference.

workItems.title: One brand timezone everywhere
workItems.problem: Lane: **cloud** builds the shared helper and the Settings part; the **browser** lane adopts it in the planner and drafts. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §18 decision 14: times appeared in different timezones on different screens. Use one brand timezone (from Klaviyo, editable in Settings) and show it next to every time: calendar, table, detail pages and the schedule step.
scope: The brand timezone comes from the connected Klaviyo account and can be changed in Settings.
One shared helper formats every date and time and names the timezone.
Calendar, table, Klaviyo detail pages, the draft editor and the schedule confirmation show the timezone next to the time.
Tests cover daylight-saving changes and a missing or invalid timezone.
workItems.doneWhen: Every owner screen that shows a time uses the one brand timezone and names it, and tests cover DST and fallback.

workItems.title: AI credits indicator and usage page
workItems.problem: Lane: **cloud**. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §18 decision 8: the old app showed a raw token strip. Show a small AI credits indicator (what is left this cycle) and a usage page that explains in plain words what used credits.
scope: Small credits indicator in the shell (the shared component exists from UIR-002).
Usage page: credits used per feature and per day this cycle, and when the cycle resets.
Owner and workspace admin only; staff see no billing numbers.
Fake provider usage only; no paid AI.
workItems.doneWhen: The owner sees credits left and a plain usage page, staff don't, and tests cover the empty cycle, a full cycle and permissions.

workItems.title: Designer workspace in the new layout
workItems.problem: Lane: **browser**, after UIR-007. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` Job 3: the designer assignment, submission and the owner's design review (including "Reject design & ask designer to redo") still use the old layout. Rebuild them in the new layout with the one status system.
scope: Designer screens: assignments list, brief, submission with files, revision requests.
Owner design review on the campaign: approve, or reject with section feedback ("Reject design & ask designer to redo") with a confirm.
Statuses use the UIR-015 words (With designer, Needs your approval).
Only the owner approves; designers see only their own assignments.
workItems.doneWhen: A designer can take an assignment and submit, the owner can approve or ask for a redo, and tests cover the owner, designer and other-designer paths.

workItems.title: Admin console screens in the new layout
workItems.problem: Lane: **cloud**, after its other M1.5 screens. The platform admin console (clients, prompts, templates, designers, operations) still uses the old layout. Rebuild it in the new layout.
scope: Clients, Prompt engine, Templates, Designers and Operations pages in the new shell and components.
Admins never creatively approve anything on behalf of an owner.
Shared loading, empty and error states; tables with keyboard access.
workItems.doneWhen: Every admin page uses the new layout, works at desktop and 375px with keyboard, and tests cover admin-only access.

workItems.title: Playwright journeys for the Top 5 owner jobs
workItems.problem: Lane: **browser**, once Campaigns and drafts land; the **cloud** lane adds the steps for its screens. `docs/OWNER_JOURNEYS.md` §1 lists five owner jobs (plan next month, make one email for a day, review copy and design then hand to a designer, approve and send to Klaviyo, see how an email is doing). Each becomes an end-to-end Playwright journey on fake providers.
scope: One journey per owner job from §1, desktop and mobile projects.
Each journey follows the checks listed under its job and asserts the honest sample/fake labels.
Runs in the Browser CI job on fake providers only.
workItems.doneWhen: All five owner jobs pass as Playwright journeys in CI on desktop and mobile.

workItems.title: 375px mobile and keyboard pass over every owner screen
workItems.problem: Lane: **whichever lane finishes its M1.5 list first**. The M1.5 goal requires every rebuilt screen to work at 375px and with the keyboard only. Do one pass over every owner screen and fix what fails.
scope: Every owner screen at 375px: no sideways scroll, readable tables, reachable actions.
Keyboard only: visible focus, sensible order, dialogs trap and return focus, Escape closes.
An automated check per screen in the Browser job (overflow and focus).
workItems.doneWhen: Every owner screen passes the 375px and keyboard checks in CI, and any failures found are fixed.

workItems.title: Retire the designer workflow (decision D3)
workItems.problem: Lane A. Decision D3: there is no designer; the AI builds every email from coded blocks. The designer desk, assignment page, owner design review and the 'With designer' status still show, and owners would wait for a designer who never comes.
scope: Hide the designer routes (desk, assignment, designer login) and the admin designer pages; links to them return Not found.
Remove designer steps from the campaign page and from every status flow: no 'With designer' pill, filter or step; old rows that still carry a designer state read in plain words.
Keep the tables and data; no destructive migration.
Update the e2e journeys that walked through the designer loop.
workItems.doneWhen: No owner, staff or admin screen shows a designer step or the 'With designer' status, the designer routes are not reachable, the designer tables are untouched, and the journeys pass.

workItems.title: Block library: 20 coded email block types and the footer
workItems.problem: Lane A. VISION.md Step 1: every email is assembled from a fixed list of block types. Claude defines the 20 types from email-marketing practice (no countdown timer in v1) and the owner approves the list.
scope: A typed list of 20 block types with plain names, a purpose line and the content each needs (text, products, image, link).
Each type renders brand-aware, email-safe HTML: logo, 3 colours and font from the brand kit, web-safe font fallback stack, tables and inline styles, 600px wide, readable at 375px.
The footer block carries Klaviyo's required tags: unsubscribe link, physical address, view in browser, organisation name.
Unit tests per block: brand values applied, no external scripts, no text inside images, size budget; a 375px and 600px rendering check.
workItems.doneWhen: All 20 types render for a sample brand at 600px and 375px with brand colours and fonts, the footer carries every required Klaviyo tag, and the owner approves the list.

workItems.title: Block gallery under Inspiration
workItems.problem: Lane A. The owner needs to see and approve the 20 block types, rendered in their own brand, before the AI uses them.
scope: A gallery page under Inspiration showing every block type in the brand's kit, at desktop and phone width, inside the sandboxed preview.
Each card shows the plain name, what it is for and what content it needs.
Works for owners and staff; sample content is labelled as sample.
workItems.doneWhen: The owner opens Inspiration, sees all 20 blocks in their brand at desktop and 375px, and can tell what each one is for.

workItems.title: Gemini adapter behind the AI port (decision D5)
workItems.problem: Lane A. Decision D5: the cheapest AI first. Google Gemini on the free tier, Flash-Lite for section labelling and classification, Flash for copy. The app only has the fake and the earlier providers.
scope: A Gemini adapter behind the existing provider-neutral AI port; model names come from configuration, not code.
The fake stays the default in tests and local runs; the live adapter needs GEMINI_API_KEY on the server and never reaches the browser.
Usage is recorded per client and a per-client spend cap refuses calls over the cap (VISION section 10).
Tests for request shape, timeouts, rate-limit and error mapping, and the cap, with no network.
workItems.doneWhen: With GEMINI_API_KEY set, a labelling call goes to Gemini Flash-Lite and its usage is recorded against the client's cap; without it, the fake answers and the app says so.

workItems.title: Section labelling harness: the model picks one of the 20 block types
workItems.problem: Lane A. VISION.md Step 1 gate: given a competitor section (image or HTML), the model's only job is to pick which of the 20 block types it is. We need a fixed-choice labeller and a way to score it against the owner's hand labels.
scope: A labeller behind the AI port that returns exactly one of the 20 type keys, or 'unsure' with low confidence (low confidence goes to the ops queue later).
A scoring harness: 50 hand-labelled sections, kept private (not in the public repository), the agreement rate and a confusion list per type.
A small admin screen where the owner labels sections and sees the score.
Runs on the fake by default; one command or button runs it on Gemini (GEM-001).
workItems.doneWhen: Gate: on the owner's 50 hand-labelled sections the model agrees at least 85% of the time; the owner reads the score and the misses on the admin screen.

workItems.title: Assemble an email from a brief: blocks, products, copy, HTML
workItems.problem: Lane A, VISION.md Step 3 (S3b). Given a hand-written brief, the AI picks a block sequence, fills product blocks from featurable products only, writes copy into each block and renders the HTML.
scope: Brief in, block sequence out (only the 20 types, no countdown), with a reason per block.
Product blocks use only featurable products with a real catalog image and price in the store currency.
Copy is written per block through the AI port; no text inside images; discount codes only from the client's list.
The rendered email is stored as a versioned campaign draft with its 375px and 600px previews.
Every step is a retryable job (three tries, then the ops queue).
workItems.doneWhen: From a hand-written brief the app produces a complete email in the brand's blocks with real products and new copy, saved as a draft the owner can preview at phone and desktop width.

workItems.title: Copy QA: facts sheet, banned words, discount regex and code list
workItems.problem: Lane A, VISION.md Step 3 (S3b) and hard rules 6 and 7. The AI must never invent free shipping, 'clinically proven', a bigger discount or a code that does not exist.
scope: Checks subject, preview and body against the brand facts sheet (shipping, returns, guarantees) and the banned words and claims.
A regex over every % and money amount refuses anything above the max discount.
Every discount code must be on the client's list and not expired.
A failed check regenerates the copy, up to three times, then goes to the ops queue; each result is stored with the email.
workItems.doneWhen: An email that promises more than the max discount, uses an unknown or expired code, or states a banned claim is blocked with a plain reason, and a clean email passes.

workItems.title: Exact, Rebrand and Adapt on blocks (decision D1)
workItems.problem: Lane A. Decision D1: Exact reproduces a competitor email's exact layout (same sections, order, proportions) with the client's own logo, colours, fonts, products, prices and new copy, never their words, images or branding. Rebrand and Adapt keep the strategy with more freedom.
scope: Exact: the labelled section sequence of a competitor email becomes the block sequence 1:1.
Rebrand: same sequence and angle, the client's brand and products, copy rewritten in their voice.
Adapt: keep the strategy and offer type, the AI may change the sequence.
Rename the old 'exact copy' path and wording to match D1; never reuse competitor text or images.
workItems.doneWhen: The owner picks a competitor email and a mode, and gets an email in their own blocks and brand that follows that mode, with no competitor words or images in it.

workItems.title: Weekly approval in the app: Approve all or Change
workItems.problem: Lane A, VISION.md Step 5. One approval covers the week's batch. The owner sees each campaign's mobile screenshot, date, offer and segment, and either approves all or asks for a change.
scope: A weekly batch view with Approve all and a Change text field per email.
Change runs at most two AI rounds, then goes to a person (ops queue).
Approved campaigns move to scheduling; 'Send test to me' and a per-campaign audience override with a warning.
Track the share approved without edits from the first client.
workItems.doneWhen: The owner approves a week's batch from their phone in one tap, a Change request is redone at most twice before a person takes over, and the approved-without-edits share is recorded.

workItems.title: Weekly approval email with signed single-use links
workItems.problem: Lane A, VISION.md Step 5 and section 10. On Sunday the client gets one email with the week's campaigns and two buttons. Replies land in the app as founder inputs; there is no no-reply address.
scope: One approval email per client per week through the email adapter (fake by default).
Approve all and Change links are signed, single-use and expire after 7 days; a used or expired link explains itself and links to the app.
Replies to the approval email are stored as founder inputs.
Tests for signing, replay, expiry, wrong tenant and the fake send.
workItems.doneWhen: The owner gets the Sunday email, taps Approve all once, and the week is approved; tapping the same link again or after 7 days does nothing and says why.

workItems.title: Hide Shopify everywhere (Klaviyo only)
workItems.problem: Lane B. v2 is Klaviyo only. Products, images, prices, orders and bestsellers come from the Klaviyo API. The app still shows Shopify on Connections, in the Store tab, in onboarding and in copy.
scope: Hide Shopify on Connections, the Store tab, onboarding, the brand check, settings and owner-facing copy.
The Store tab shows Klaviyo catalog data, or nothing, never Shopify.
No new Shopify code. Keep tables and adapters (no destructive migrations).
workItems.doneWhen: No owner or staff screen offers or mentions connecting Shopify. Tests cover the hidden routes and copy. `pnpm verify` is green. The ledger has a handoff entry.

workItems.title: Inspiration inbox: Gmail IMAP transport and brand assignment
workItems.problem: Lane B. Competitor emails are fixture-only. v2 needs real newsletters. For now (D4) they arrive at `ramangreyofficial+<brand-slug>@gmail.com` and are read over IMAP.
scope: An `InboundCaptureTransport` port with a fake (the default) and a Gmail IMAP adapter. A catch-all domain can replace Gmail later without other changes.
The scheduled worker polls the inbox through the job system. The work is idempotent: the message id is never processed twice.
The brand comes from the +alias slug, then from the sender domain. Anything else goes to the ops queue.
Each captured email stores its raw MIME and HTML as a real (non-synthetic) capture.
Credentials come only from `INBOX_IMAP_USER` and `INBOX_IMAP_APP_PASSWORD` on the server. They are never in code, logs or chat.
workItems.doneWhen: The fake transport delivers sample emails end to end. The IMAP adapter is unit-tested against a recorded session. Tests cover: assignment by alias, by sender, unknown sender, no duplicates and the failure paths. `pnpm verify` and `test:db` are green.

workItems.title: Inspiration inbox: keep every image at once and a 600px screenshot
workItems.problem: Lane B. Tracking and image URLs in newsletters expire. We must keep every image as soon as an email arrives, and keep a picture of the whole email.
scope: On arrival, download every image the HTML references into private storage. Record size, type and source, and handle failures and size limits.
Render the email at 600px wide, sandboxed with links off, and save a full-height screenshot.
Both run as idempotent jobs. A retry never stores anything twice.
workItems.doneWhen: A captured email shows its stored images and its screenshot in Inspiration. Tests cover: broken images, oversized files, non-image responses, and a retry that stores nothing twice. `pnpm verify` and `test:db` are green.

workItems.title: Inspiration extraction: sections, text/design, micro and macro facts, repetition
workItems.problem: Lane B. A stored email teaches nothing until it is broken into sections and facts.
scope: Find section boundaries from the HTML structure (table rows, image slices). The model only labels sections; it does not find them.
Label each section text or design, and give the email a text:design ratio.
Micro facts per email: subject, preview, offer, angle, CTA, send day and time (brand timezone), block sequence.
Macro facts per brand: frequency, campaign-type mix, discount depth and pattern, text:design ratio.
Repetition weighting: a pattern that repeats counts more than a one-off.
Each email is processed once; its labels are stored and never reprocessed. Labelling goes through the provider-neutral AI port, fake by default.
workItems.doneWhen: A brand page shows its summary, made from its own emails. Tests cover section splitting on real-shaped HTML, the facts, the weighting, and process-once. `pnpm verify` and `test:db` are green. Gate (owner): 200 emails assigned and labelled correctly, plus a per-brand summary the owner agrees with.

workItems.title: Inbox ops queue and admin brand directory
workItems.problem: Lane B. A person must see what the inbox could not handle. The owner subscribes to competitors by hand and needs each brand's address.
scope: An inbox ops queue covering: unknown sender; parse failure; double-opt-in confirmations (links matching "confirm" are clicked by the worker only for known brands, and every click is logged); brands that unsubscribed us (a resubscribe task); pending subscriptions
An admin brand directory: each competitor brand with its `+alias` address, niche, subscription status and last email received.
Admin only, through RLS and server checks.
workItems.doneWhen: An admin sees the queue and the directory, and can resolve a task. Tests cover authorization (owners and staff refused), every task type and the resolve path. `pnpm verify` and `test:db` are green.

workItems.title: Live Klaviyo adapter: key scopes, catalog, bestsellers, scheduled campaigns, Engaged segment
workItems.problem: Lane B. Everything comes from Klaviyo, but today only a fake adapter exists.
scope: A live Klaviyo adapter behind the existing `klaviyo-read` port. The fake stays the default.

The adapter covers: the key's scopes checked on paste, with the exact missing scopes shown; the account's timezone and currency; the catalog cached and cleaned: variant suffixes stripped, variants grouped into one product, currency checked, an image required; a block with a clear message when the catalog is empty; bestsellers from Placed Order events, cached weekly; existing scheduled campaigns read, so those days count as taken; the Engaged 90 days segment created, or Engaged 180 days when 90 days gives fewer than 1,000 profiles or under 20% of the list
Rate limits and expired or revoked keys go to the ops queue, and generation pauses.
Every step is an idempotent job that retries 3 times.
workItems.doneWhen: Contract tests against recorded Klaviyo responses pass. A live call happens only when the owner pastes a real key. Tests cover the failure paths (bad key, missing scope, empty catalog, rate limit). `pnpm verify` and `test:db` are green.

workItems.title: Onboarding wizard (VISION §5 and §10)
workItems.problem: Lane B. Onboarding is the most important screen. It collects everything the AI may use, and nothing else.
scope: A step-by-step wizard: 1. Klaviyo key, with the scope check and a guide. 2. Max discount %. 3. Discount codes (code, %, expiry). Zero codes is allowed. 4. Blackout dates. 5. Store timezone and currency, read from Klaviyo. 6. Send frequency: 2, 3 or 4 a week. 7. Brand kit: logo, 3 colours and a font, scraped and then shown visually for confirmation. 8. Brand facts sheet: shipping, returns, guarantees, banned words and claims, tone as 3 chips. It is pre-filled by scraping those pages. 9. Featurable products, pre-ticked: the top 20 bestsellers plus anything added in the last 30 days. 10. 5–10 competitors, suggested by niche and similar size. When there are none, cold-start mode, said plainly.
It checks for a dedicated sending domain and flags it without blocking.
It tells the owner that pushed templates are edited through Change.
When it finishes, the post-onboarding job chain starts and shows progress.
workItems.doneWhen: The owner can finish onboarding at 375px, with the keyboard. Each step's answer is saved and can be resumed. Tests cover validation, authorization and failure paths. `pnpm verify`, `test:db` and `test:e2e` are green.

workItems.title: Full QA before Klaviyo push (VISION Step 4)
workItems.problem: Lane B. Nothing may reach a client's Klaviyo account unless it passes every hard check.
scope: Each of these checks blocks the push when it fails:
Every link returns 200 and matches the intended product.
The discount code is in the client's list, not expired, and no more than the max.
The send date is not a blackout date and not already taken by another campaign.
Every featured product exists and is featurable.
The HTML is under 102KB, so Gmail does not clip it.
A 375px screenshot renders cleanly. The approval screen reuses it.
The copy passes the facts sheet and the banned-words list.
The audience is the Engaged segment.
The send time is converted from the store's timezone. Results are stored per campaign in `qa_results` and shown in words.
workItems.doneWhen: Each check has passing and failing tests. A failure blocks the push and says why. `pnpm verify` and `test:db` are green.

workItems.title: Klaviyo push as draft
workItems.problem: Lane B. Approved, QA-passed emails must land in the client's Klaviyo account.
scope: The push runs in this order: upload images to Klaviyo, create the template, create the campaign, assign the Engaged segment, save it as a **draft**.
No scheduling: that comes only after Step 5 proves approval.
Idempotent jobs with 3 retries, then the ops queue.
Hourly status sync: a campaign edited or deleted outside the app is marked "externally modified" and never overwritten.
The fake adapter is the default; live calls only with the owner's key.
workItems.doneWhen: Contract tests against recorded Klaviyo responses pass. Tests cover partial-failure retries (no duplicate templates or campaigns) and externally modified campaigns. `pnpm verify` and `test:db` are green. Gate (owner): 10 of 10 drafts land in Klaviyo with zero manual fixes.

workItems.title: Ops dashboard (VISION §10)
workItems.problem: Lane B. The platform team needs one daily view of every client and every task waiting for a person.
scope: Every client, with: next send; approval status; QA failures; last results; days since competitor data was refreshed; LLM spend against its cap
The ops queue across every source: inbox; low-confidence labels; copy QA failed 3 times; Change requests past 2 rounds; Klaviyo API errors
Admin only.
workItems.doneWhen: An admin sees every client and can open and resolve tasks. Tests cover authorization and every task source. `pnpm verify` and `test:db` are green.
